ryan: Heads up — nightly perf CI small-batch latency job regressed after driver 551 landed in staging. p95 jumped ~30% for seq<=32, batch=1.
ci-bot: [smallseq-latency] job failed on 2145678899 (regression +31% p95) — marking as flaky/regression.
maggie: saw a similar spike on the canary cluster a few minutes ago, 2x the usual p50 for tiny requests. Not a traffic anomaly.
oli: any recent changes in autotune or kernel selection? we didn't merge runtime changes in the last deploy AFAIK.
ryan: nothing on our side — but infra bumped NVIDIA driver -> 551.22 last night across staging nodes.
devon: ops confirmed the driver bump; rolling back to 550 on a small node pool now to A/B.
marie: profiled the failing endpoint with nsys, here's the hot part: ```
# top by GPU time
matmul_v2_small_kernel  48.2%  12.3ms
matmul_generic         21.7%  5.6ms
softmax_fused          12.1%  3.1ms
memcpy_htod             8.0%  2.0ms
```
marie: interestingly, matmul_v2_small_kernel latency increased ~2.3x compared to baseline (driver 550). L2 miss rate also up.
maggie: nvprof snapshot shows different PTX path chosen for same kernel with driver 551 — kernel selector seems to pick `matmul_v2_small` for compute capability 8.6+, whereas before it picked `matmul_tile_32`.
ryan: I started a git bisect across recent merges touching autotune/kernel selector. narrowed to PR #4123 (autorouting: prefer 'small' matmul when seq<64 && batch<=2).
oli: PR #4123 landed 3 days ago — the heuristic seemed fine on our microbench but maybe driver/PTX changes interact badly.
devon: can we quickly revert the heuristic change as a rollout blocker for the hosted fleet? Canary rollback to driver 550 is slow.
ryan: opened revert PR #4170 and queued a canary patch that pins the selector to the previous path for affected shapes. Also added a perf gate to CI to catch smallbatch p95 regressions.
ops-bot: Revert PR #4170 pushed to staging pool-2 at 2145679140. Canary metrics: smallseq p95 back to baseline within 2 runs. :white_check_mark:
marie: filing an upstream bug with NVIDIA — attaching nsys trace and diffed kernels. Also adding a regression unit to the autotune test harness that asserts chosen kernel and p95.
maggie: follow-ups: (1) keep driver 551 on non-prod for now, (2) add CI perf test for batch=1 seq=8/16/32, (3) adjust selector heuristic to prefer stable paths when driver version >=551 until we get NV feedback.
oli: thanks — once revert lands we'll roll the revert to prod canary and re-run the full perf job matrix.
ryan: TL;DR: driver 551 changed PTX/runtime behavior -> kernel selector favored a faster-looking path that regressed in practice; bisect -> PR #4123 heuristic + driver interaction; revert PR #4170 merged to unblock rollout; follow-ups tracked in #perf-regressions board.
marie: added label `regression/driver-551` and assigned to ryan + maggie.
devon: adding oncall ping @oncall for visibility in case any customer-facing latency pops up overnight.
ryan: thanks everyone — keeping this thread for final perf numbers after the revert finishes canary.
